note: One of the six groups in the closed budget every world in a universe competes to hold.
A slot only means something because the six-group supply it draws on is finite and shared.
A boundary is only definable between two holders of the same budget; two different vocabularies would not produce a disagreement, they would produce nothing comparable.
A universe is the possibility-space of imprints; without imprints it is a list of six names.
An imprint is held by one layer, which is where the authored law list lives.
Qi Law is the archetypal imprintable group: its authored 0.1-100 range makes presence a dial reading rather than a yes.
One imprint costs one slot; a budget is nothing but a count of these.
A layer is the only structural unit that sits inside a universe, because a universe is not a place.
An authored WorldLayerState carries its own law list; a region with no laws is a region, not a layer.
Fifteen imprints over six groups cannot sit in one layer, so the top tier is layered by arithmetic.
Three imprints need one layer, so a mortal world is single-layered and its surface list is its whole law set.
The budget is a count, and the thing counted is an imprint.
Three imprints over six groups is the tightest budget in the setting and the origin of every limit in the lowest tier.
Fifteen imprints is the loosest budget and the reason the top tier is limited by will rather than by supply.
Three slots against six groups is what leaves three groups unwritten in the lowest tier.
Six slots equals the six authored groups, which is what makes the second tier the first with nothing merely unspent.
Ten imprints over six groups leaves four duplicates, which is what forces the second layer.
Fifteen imprints need three law lists, which is what makes a world this size built rather than grown.
A realm band ends where a tier's imprints run out, so the four authored bands are a consequence of the four budgets.
Elemental Law is the group a three-slot world drops first, because nothing a mortal tier holds needs an element.
Gathering three groups into one body is affordable only where the budget has imprints to spare, which starts at the immortal tier.
This is the law profile of the lowest authored tier, and the profile is what the three slots buy.
Iron ore, common herb and beast inhabitants are exactly what physical, life and qi buy; nothing there needs an element.
The deficiency is defined against the profile: it is the third group on the unspent list, not a free-standing curse.
Qi Law is spent here at the floor of its 0.1-100 range, which is what strained means in a place with no spare slots.
The law profile of the second authored tier, where six slots finally match the six authored groups.
Spirit stone and jade ore with beast and humanoid inhabitants are what a full six-group set produces at this size.
Qi Dao's home tier is derived from this profile: it is the first one where qi, temporal and element reach working values together.
Ten imprints over six groups, at least two layers, and the first budget that can concentrate three groups in one place.
Immortal essence, star metal and a humanoid-plus-elemental population are the outputs of that concentration, at danger level 8.
An elemental needs three groups in one body, and this is the first profile whose budget can gather them.
Fifteen imprints across three layers, and the only profile where the shortage is the holder rather than the supply.
Dao fragment and void crystal with a humanoid-plus-elemental population are what fifteen imprints leave behind at danger level 10.
A single unified Dao needs all six groups legible at once, which only this budget affords.
A void is the shape of unspent slots; without a budget there is nothing to have failed to buy.
Three of the six groups are unwritten in the lowest tier, and this is what an unwritten group does to a place.
The elemental case is the worked example: one group, all three absence signatures, a named tier.
Removing an imprint from a layer that held one does not restore the layer; it leaves the outline behind.
A scar is the negative space inside a specific layer, not a mood spread across a world.
A scar is the memory of one imprint, so a world that never held the group cannot scar.
Qi Law at 0.1 is the canonical strained case: enough for breath and a five-point strike, not enough for a dantian.
Strained means present at the floor of an authored range, so there is a dial and only the dial is pinned.
A tide is only worth having where the floor is fixed, because it is the only cheap way off that floor.
A qi reading wired to the floor pushes practitioners toward a form-only practice, which is what makes that heresy reproducible rather than eccentric.
Concentration is a budget question: three groups have to be affordable in one place, not merely present in a world.
The phenomenon occurs exactly where the budget first allows it, and the authored storm elemental names the same two tiers.
The same group, unwritten in the tier below and concentrated in this one; elemental life is a function of concentration, not of altitude.
Returning to a home tier meets the scar left by the departure, which is the price a migrating Dao pays on every circuit.
Mortal worlds license no humanoid, so Body Dao's home tier cannot produce its own practitioners and migration is forced rather than chosen.
Migrating Body Dao arrives where qi is already spent, and what it becomes there is a doctrine with the qi component removed.
Three slots against a three-group subset places Body Dao's home in the lowest tier, which the authored data confirms and this derives.
Six slots are the first budget carrying qi, temporal and element at working values, which is why Qi Dao's home is the second tier.
Spatial Law read at the high end needs a container larger than a self, which only the top tier's size and budget hold.
Body Dao is one of the three self-sufficient readings; the count of three is bounded by the six-group vocabulary, not by history.
Qi Dao is the reading that fits a six-slot spirit world without strain, and the only one with a native population.
Mind Dao is the reading that needs spatial at the top of its range, so it is native to the top tier and nowhere cheaper.
Each reading needs its own three-group subset, and three subsets is what a six-slot world can hold without them competing.
Its three-group subset is exactly a mortal tier's three slots, which is why it is native there with nothing to spare.
Its subset needs a budget that also carries element, and the six-slot spirit tier is the first one that does.
Its subset needs spatial read high, and only the fifteen-slot top tier affords a container bigger than the self leaving it.
A Dao is a local reading of an imprinted group, so its content is a function of the world's law values rather than of a founder.
Same mechanism from the other side: the same principle reads differently where spatial is at the floor and where it is at the ceiling.
A reading cannot crystallise around a group no layer holds, which is why a mortal tier has no Dao of its own to have.
Every Dao in the setting is a reading of the same six groups, so the vocabulary is shared and only the values differ.
It is Body Dao's form-permanence claim with the qi component removed, arrived at independently by practitioners who could not draw qi.
A void does not merely restrict practice, it invents one: with no qi to spend, a form-only doctrine is the reading that survives.
Its reproducibility comes from the mortal profile: a three-slot world where qi is spent at the floor pushes everyone the same way.
A realm is a range of tolerated pressure, so it is measured against imprints rather than against effort.
Realms 1-9 end where three imprints run out, which makes the ceiling a property of the world rather than a verdict on a student.
Realms 28-30 end because thirty realms are authored; that edge is a content decision and not a cosmological one.
A tide carries the band's pressure up briefly, so a realm can be touched at a crest and not held in the trough.
Tide cycles are named in Qi Law's own authored description, and its 0.1-100 range is the amplitude they move through.
Where qi is not spent at the floor, a tide still governs when a breakthrough is attempted.
A tide on a 0.1 qi reading is too thin to cultivate on and too real to ignore; it is a mortal's whole life as trough with brief crests.
A surge that reaches the end of the authored range is out of range, and an out-of-range imprint stops holding and tears.
Crossing is leaving one imprint list for another, so a boundary is only a problem where the lists differ.
A realm band is a band of one world's values, so the higher a body is tuned the more brittle it is across a boundary.
A rift is the only place a boundary is locally present, which is what makes adjacency the exception and isolation the norm.
A tear is a failed imprint; a world with nothing overpressed has nothing to fail.
Fifteen imprints across three layers with temporal readable to 100 is fifteen chances to push a dial off its end.
Tides set the cycle a tear opens and closes on, which is why no rift in the setting has outlasted a few tides.
A Dao is native to the lowest tier its three-group subset fits, and exiled everywhere else; the ladder of home tiers is the migration map.
